$> export HOSTTYPE=Testing $> make re ... $> ln -s libft_malloc_Testing.so libft_malloc.so $> ls -l libft_malloc.so libft_malloc.so -> libft_malloc_Testing.so $>

sections.note:

FOR MAC:
$> cat run.sh

$>

body.text: Create a script named run.sh and make it executable:

FOR LINUX:

Yes
No
We are first going to make a first test program that does not use malloc, so that we have a base to compare to.
Use test0.c file attached in the scale
WARNING: If you are using a linux vm, make sure that you are using the time binary that you can get with apt (sudo apt install time), else you won't have access to the -v option

MAC: $> gcc -o test0 test0.c $> /usr/bin/time -l ./test0 0.00 LINUX: $> gcc -o test0 test0.c $> /usr/bin/time -v ./test0 0.00 Command being timed: "./test0" User time (seconds): 0.00 System time (seconds): 0.00 Percent of CPU this job got: 0% Elapsed (wall clock) time (h:mm:ss or m:ss): 0:00.00 Average shared text size (kilobytes): 0 Average unshared data size (kilobytes): 0 Average stack size (kilobytes): 0 Average total size (kilobytes): 0 Maximum resident set size (kilobytes): 412 Average resident set size (kilobytes): 0 Major (requiring I/O) page faults: 0 Minor (reclaiming frame) page faults: 130 Voluntary context switches: 0 Involuntary context switches: 0 Swaps: 0 File system inputs: 0 File system outputs: 0 Socket messages sent: 0 Socket messages received: 0 Signals delivered: 0 Page size (bytes): 4096 Exit status: 0 $>

We will then add malloc and write in each allocation to make sure that the memory page is allocated in physical memory by MMU. The system will only really allocate the memory of page if you write in it, so even if we do a bigger mmap than the malloc request it won't modify the "page reclaims".
Using the test1.c file given as attachment, run the following tests:

$> gcc -o test1 test1.c $> /usr/bin/time -l ./test1 (Use -v for linux) Command being timed: "./test1" User time (seconds): 0.00 System time (seconds): 0.00 Percent of CPU this job got: 0% Elapsed (wall clock) time (h:mm:ss or m:ss): 0:00.00 Average shared text size (kilobytes): 0 Average unshared data size (kilobytes): 0 Average stack size (kilobytes): 0 Average total size (kilobytes): 0 Maximum resident set size (kilobytes): 1500 Average resident set size (kilobytes): 0 Major (requiring I/O) page faults: 0 Minor (reclaiming frame) page faults: 402 Voluntary context switches: 0 Involuntary context switches: 0 Swaps: 0 File system inputs: 0 File system outputs: 0 Socket messages sent: 0 Socket messages received: 0 Signals delivered: 0 Page size (bytes): 4096 Exit status: 0

Our test1 program requested 1024 times 1024 bytes, so 1Mb. We can therefore check by doing the difference with the test0 program:
- either between the "maximum resident set size" lines, we obtain a little more than 1Mb
- or between the page reclaims lines that we will multiply by the value of getpagesize(3)
Let's test now both programs with our library:

$>./run.sh /usr/bin/time -l ./test0 (Use -v for linux) ... Maximum resident set size (kilobytes): 412 Minor (reclaiming frame) page faults: 130 ... $>./run.sh /usr/bin/time -l ./test1 (Use -v for linux) ... Maximum resident set size (kilobytes): 1984 Minor (reclaiming frame) page faults: 525 $>
Count the number of pages used and adjust the grade as such:

items: less than 255 pages, allocated memory is insufficient: 0
1023 pages and over, the malloc works but consumes 1 page minimum for each allocation: 1
between 513 pages and 1022 pages, malloc works but the overhead is too big: 2
between 313 pages and 512 pages, malloc works but the overhead is very big: 3
between 273 pages and 312 pages, malloc works but the overhead is big: 4
between 255 and 272 pages, malloc works and the overhead is fine: 5

Check inside the source code that the pre-allocated zones for the different malloc sizes allow to store at least 100 times the maximum size for this type of zone. Check also that the size of the zones is a multiple of getpagesize().

test2 has at most 3 more "page reclaims" than test0?

body.text: Before evaluation starts, make sure that:

body.text:

Before running the program, run the following command: `rm
-f /var/lock/matt_daemon.lock ; rm -rf /var/log/matt_daemon/`.
Run the program as the root user.

The "netstat -tulpn" command will allow you to check that the 4242 port
is in LISTEN mode.

The /var/lock/matt_daemon.lock and /var/log/matt_daemon/matt_daemon.log
files are available.

and make a kill -15 (daemon's PID).

-f /var/lock/matt_daemon.lock ; rm -rf /var/log/matt_daemon/`.
Run the program with the root rights.
Use the netcat command to connect to the daemon ("nc localhost 4242").

questions.name: Ex04, evalexpr is so easy it hurts

body.text:
This exercice is very representative of OCaml. Writing an
evalexpr in C or C++ is at best painful. With OCaml, it's easy
and elegant.

Given the signature VAL and the description of the EVALEXPR
signature, this signature must be similar to the following.
module type EVALEXPR = sig type t type expr = | Add of (expr * expr) | Mul of (expr * expr) | Value of t val eval : expr -> t end

The types VAL.t and EVALEXPR.t beeing abstract, the MAKEEVALEXPR
functor signature must include a constraint sharing on those
types.
module type MAKEEVALEXPR = functor (Val:VAL) -> EVALEXPR with type t = Val.t * OR * module type MAKEEVALEXPR = functor (Val:VAL) -> EVALEXPR with type t := Val.t

I won't give out the implementation of the functor MakeEvalExpr
as it is a very good programming exercice. Don't forget to check
that this functor actually implements the MAKEEVALEXPR
signature, obviously.

The six addtionnal constraint sharing from the last part of the
exercice are the following.

module IntVal : (VAL with type t = int) = <...> module FloatVal : (VAL with type t = float) = <...> module StringVal : (VAL with type t = string) = <...> module IntEvalExpr : (EVALEXPR with type t = IntVal.t ) = <...> module FloatEvalExpr : (EVALEXPR with type t = FloatVal.t ) = <...> module StringEvalExpr : (EVALEXPR with type t = StringVal.t ) = <...>
The four destructive substitution are the following.

module type MAKEEVALEXPR = functor (Val:VAL) -> EVALEXPR with type t := Val.t module IntEvalExpr : (EVALEXPR with type t := IntVal.t ) = <...> module FloatEvalExpr : (EVALEXPR with type t := FloatVal.t ) = <...> module StringEvalExpr : (EVALEXPR with type t := StringVal.t ) = <...>
Also, check that the output is good.

Res = 42
Res = 42.420000
Res = very very long
$>

Obviously, incorrect values of n must be handled correctly (with
an exception for instance, but anything is fine as long as it
makes sense). There must also be at least methane (1), ethane
(2) and octane (8) implemented.

All the methods specified in the exercise (get_start,
get_result, balance, is_balanced) have to be present with the
right types (these methods are all virtual). As a consequence,
there is nothing really to test, but if the student made a dummy
reaction class and tested it that is really a great idea.

This is where it gets hard. There has to be a class named
alkane_combustion, and there are basically two states. First you
instantiate the class with a list of alkanes; but that
combustion is not balanced yet, so get_start and get_result
throw an exception, and is_balanced return false. Then you call
balance on it, which returns a new object. This combustion has
to be balanced, is_balanced has to return true, and get_start
and get_result have to return consistent results (they have to
make up a really balanced alkane combustion.)

This is a new method on the alkane_combustion class. It has to
be named get_incomplete_results, and return an associative list.
The index will be the quantity of molecular oxygen at the start
of the combustion, and the value will be the different possible
outcomes. Check that all the results are valid, without
duplicates, and comprehensive (if you can find a solution which
is not included in the function's returned value, the exercise
is obviously incorrect).

Error management

Try the program without any parameter, with too many parameters, with
invalid parameters, with invalid sequences... Try to make it fault. Does

Simple position

Try the program with simple mixes with no more than 4-5 spins. Is the
result correct? Does it appear in a reasonable period (2-3 seconds)? If
the answer to one of theses questions is no, evaluation stops.
Complex position

Try the program with more complex mixes, between 5 and 20 spins. Is the
result correct? Does it appear in a reasonable period (2-3 seconds)? If
the answer to one of theses questions is no, evaluation stops.
Random position

Try the program with random mixes, more than 20 spins scale. Is the result
correct? Does it appear in a reasonable period (2-3 seconds)? If the
answer to one of theses questions is no, evaluation stops.
Performance

For the mixes superior than 30 spins, can the program solve them in
an average number of spins below 150 and still below 2-3 seconds, including
display? If the answer is no, give 0 for this question. Add 1 point for
each slice of 20 spins earned.
Distance-20

U R2 F B R B2 R U2 L B2 R U' D' R2 F R' L B2 U2 F2. This position
called superflip, are parts of the positions that always require at least
20 spins to be solved ("Distance-20"). Does the program resolve this

sections.note: An app without an icon is not an app!

body.text:

screen that remains visible for at least 1 second.

sections.title: First View
sections.note: Login View!

body.text:
Verify that the project compiles, uses modern layout techniques, and launches
the simulator correctly. If any of these requirements are not met, the
evaluation stops here.

Verify that users can create an account and log in using biometric authentication
(Face ID/Touch ID on iOS, BiometricPrompt on Android).
Once the user logs in successfully, the next view should load.

If biometric authentication fails, verify that a popup alerts the user
that authentication has failed.
Verify that passwords are handled securely:

items: Ask the student to explain how passwords are stored
Confirm that passwords are NOT stored in plain text
Verify that appropriate hashing or platform-specific secure storage is used (e.g., Keychain on iOS, KeyStore on Android, or hashing algorithms like bcrypt)

body.text: If passwords are stored in plain text, this is a critical security flaw.

If the device does not support biometric authentication, verify that
the user can log in using a username and password.

The application must always prompt the user to log in when accessing
the app, even if they haven't logged out but have navigated away
(e.g., by returning to the home screen) and then returned to it.

Verify that the following steps work correctly:
1) Launch the application and confirm the Login View is displayed.
2) Log in to the app and navigate to the next view.
3) Press the home button to return to the home screen.
4) Launch the application again and confirm the Login View is displayed.
If the Login View is not displayed, the application is not secure.

sections.title: Second View
sections.note: List View

body.text: Verify that all ligands listed in the ligands.txt file are displayed in the list.
Verify that you can search for a ligand using the search bar.

items: Confirm that when a ligand is selected, the correct ligand loads!

body.text:
If the application fails to load a ligand, verify that a warning popup appears
indicating the reason for the failure (e.g., no network, wrong URL, etc.).

Note: The application is expected to fetch ligand data from an open and publicly
available source, using a suitable file format.
The .cif format from RCSB is provided as a reference example.
Other open and publicly available file formats commonly used to represent proteins
(such as .sdf) are also acceptable, as long as they correctly represent protein
structures and are compatible with the project requirements.

Verify that a spinning wheel (or clean loading animation) is displayed
while the ligand is loading.

sections.title: Third View
sections.note: Protein View

body.text:
Verify that the ligand is displayed using 3D in-app rendering (SceneKit
on iOS, or appropriate 3D framework on Android), and that you can zoom
in/out and rotate the model to view it from different angles.
Verify that the ligand is displayed using the Ball-and-Stick model with CPK coloring.

Verify that when the user taps an atom, a tooltip or popup displays the
atom type. The tooltip should disappear when the user taps anywhere else
on the screen. The tooltip must display information about the atom, such
as its symbol (e.g., C for carbon, H for hydrogen, O for oxygen, etc.).
Also verify that the 3D model supports smooth gesture controls:

items: Rotation: Drag/swipe to rotate the molecule
Zoom: Pinch gesture to zoom in/out
Pan (optional): Two-finger drag to move the camera

body.text: All gestures should be smooth and responsive without lag.

Verify that you can share the model using the share button and save it
to your photo album.

items:
Verify that the student has implemented additional molecular visualization
models beyond the mandatory Ball-and-Stick model.

Confirm that users can switch between different models (e.g., Space-Filling,
Wireframe, Stick) using a UI control.
Test that switching between models works smoothly without reloading the molecule.

Verify that each model is correctly implemented according to molecular
visualization standards.
Evaluate any additional bonus features the student has implemented.

Consider features such as:
Advanced UI/UX (custom cells, animations, dark mode)
Enhanced interactions (atom highlighting, measurement tools)
Performance optimizations (caching, smooth 60 FPS)
Extended sharing (custom messages, multiple formats)
Award points based on the quality, usefulness, and implementation of these features.
Remember: Bonuses are only evaluated if the mandatory part is perfect.

body.text:
Le programme fournit plusieurs commandes shell sympathique, soit
dans le programme lui même ou dans un programme séparé (comme
supervisorctl). Le shell permet de démarrer, arrêter, et
redémarrer le programme.

Le programme charge sa configuration depuis le fichier de
configuration, peut importe le format. Pour cette
fonctionnalité, les librairies externes (comme la librairie de
parsing YAML, par exemple) sont autorisées. Le programme
décrit dans le fichier de configuration est actuelement
chargé, ses statuts peuvent etre cosultés avec le shell,
etc...

Ceci est un systeme de log, qui se connecte à un fichier (Plus
de point dans la section bonus). Pour que ce soit vrai, il doit
y avoir un nombre raisonnable d'evenements pris en consideration
: Quand les programmes sont démarrés, arrêtés, redémarrés,
quand ils s'arrêtent de façon inattendus, Quand le projet
aborts au lancement à cause d'un nombre trop important d'essai,
etc...

La configuration peut être rechargé tant que le programme est
lancé, à la fois avec un SIGHUP et avec une commande shell.
Lorsque le reload prend effet, l'état du programme doit être
modifié pour être conforme à sa nouvelle configuration.
Cependant, les programmes qui ne sont pas affectés par le
changement de configuration ne doivent en aucun cas être
redémarrés (Ca serait très, très bâclé)

- If the correcting student has not completed that particular project yet, it is mandatory for this student to read the entire subject prior to starting the defence.

- Use the flags available on this scale to signal an empty repository, non-functioning program, norm error, cheating etc. In these cases, the grading is over and the final grade is 0 (or -42 in case of cheating). However, with the exception of cheating, you are encouraged to continue to discuss your work (even if you have not finished it) in order to identify any issues that may have caused this failure and avoid repeating the same mistake in the future.

- The evaluation must take place in a virtual machine under Linux with a kernel > 3.14 and admin (root) rights.

body.text: First, check that the following is true:

items: Something has been uploaded to the GiT repository.
The project is written in C (or possibly in ASM).
There is a Makefile and it contains the usual rules.

body.text: If any of the above is not true, the defence ends. You are still, however, encouraged to continue to discuss the project.
Before running the program, run the following command:
echo "int main(void){ printf(\"Hello\\n\"); return 0;}" > hello.c; gcc -m64 -o hello hello.c
Then run the program with the 'hello' binary passed as the first parameter.
There should now be a new file named 'woody'.
If that is not the case, the project is incomplete and the defence ends.
Run 'woody'.
The program should first output "....WOODY....", followed by a newline and "Hello".
If that is not the case, the defence ends.
Run the following command:
objdump -S woody > woody.obj ; objdump -S hello > hello.obj
You may now diff (hello.obj and woody.obj) with your favorite software and see that there are many differences.
If that is not the case, the defence ends.
Note by scale of how clear the algorithm is to the corrector after an explanation from the student.
Understand how the algorithm can be improved. What pros and cons come with use of the algorithm.

A maximum score should only be given if the corrector completely understands the algorithm after the explanation (or at the very least if the corrector is 100% certain that the student completely understands what they are talking about).
Note by scale of difficulty/effectiveness of the chosen algorithm.
The student must explain and justify their choice of algorithm.
A simple ROT is not considered a complex algorithm!
A maximum score should only be given in the case of a complex algorithm that creates a unique random key generated at runtime of the main executable.
Before running the program, run the following command:
echo "int main(void){ printf(\"Hello\n\"); return 0;}" > hello.c; gcc -m32 -o hello hello.c
Then run the program with the 'hello' binary passed as the first parameter.
The program should either display an explicit error message, or in the case of a bonus, work as intended without any issues.
The corrector may then run the program with as many error cases as they can think of (invalid file, invalid path, not enough permissions, etc...).

sections.title: Bonus
sections.note: Bonus will be taken into account only if ALL the previous points are valid.

body.text: All bonuses must be 100% functional and useful/convenient to be counted.
Examples of valid bonuses:

items: 32bit support.
Custom keys.
Optimization of the algorithm used by the assembler.
Support of multiple binary formats (PE, Mach-O, ...).
Compression of the binary.

sheets.name: Work Experience - Company Mid Evaluation
sheets.introduction:
This form allows you to evaluate the learner midway through their
professional experience within your company.
We recommend completing this evaluation in the learner’s presence
whenever possible.

The goal is to assess their progress during the first few months
of their professional experience:
- What went well?
- How well have they integrated into the team?
- What skills were expected, and how has the learner met those
expectations?

This is also an opportunity for the learner to share their impressions:
- Do they feel integrated?
- Are they satisfied with the workload, the technologies used,
the work environment, and the tasks assigned?
sheets.guidelines:
This document follows the 42 evaluation structure. You must evaluate
each point based on the learner’s performance.
You should also write a final comment summarizing your evaluation,
which will be visible to the learner.

This evaluation should be completed with the learner whenever possible
and should encourage constructive feedback and discussion.

Each question is graded on a scale from 0 to 5.

items: Did the learner's technical skills meet your expectations?
Were they consistent with or better than those presented during the recruitment process?

body.text:
Rating (0 to 5): unacceptable, very insufficient, insufficient,
adequate, good, excellent

Assess the learner’s ability to stay organized and work
independently:

items: Do they follow your company’s organization(e.g., working hours, dress code)?
Are they autonomous and proactive (e.g., seeking documentation or asking colleagues when needed)?

body.text:
Rating (0 to 5): unacceptable, very insufficient, insufficient,
adequate, good, excellent

items: Has the learner found their place within the team?
Do they maintain good relationships with colleagues?

body.text:
Rating (0 to 5): unacceptable, very insufficient, insufficient,
adequate, good, excellent

items: Has the learner contributed effectively to the assigned tasks or projects?

body.text:
Rating (0 to 5): unacceptable, very insufficient, insufficient,
adequate, good, excellent

items: How would you rate the learner’s creativity?

body.text:
Creativity may be expressed in various ways:
suggesting technical options, offering relevant alternatives,
or proposing unconventional yet effective solutions.

Rating (0 to 5): unacceptable, very insufficient, insufficient,
adequate, good, excellent

items: What is your overall impression of the learner’s performance during their time in the company?

body.text:
This question summarizes the previous ones and plays a major role
in determining the final grade for their work experience.

Rating (0 to 5): unacceptable, very insufficient, insufficient,
adequate, good, excellent
For statistical purposes only (not included in the final grade):

items: To what extent do you believe the learner is ready to enter the professional world?

As usual, clone the Git repository of the learner you are evaluating.
It must contain a file with a link to the video hosted on a platform
such as YouTube, Dailymotion, etc.

This evaluation can be completed without the presence of the person
being evaluated. However, if this is abused, mandatory attendance
will be reinstated.

If there is no link, the video cannot be viewed and the evaluation
ends here.

Please note that some videos may be "censored" for confidentiality
reasons. Not everything can be shared in full. Proceed thoughtfully.
Even if some parts are not explained in detail, the content and
overall logic must remain understandable.
The video lasts approximately 5 minutes (±1 minute tolerance).

The video includes a presentation made using appropriate software
(PowerPoint, Prezi, Keynote, MagicPoint, etc.).
The visual and audio quality is acceptable (not pixelated, muffled, or inaudible).

The learner's face is visible for most of the video. (It is acceptable
to include intro/conclusion segments or chapters where the learner is
in close-up, or temporarily off-screen to display a title.)

The overall presentation is professional:
--> No distracting fonts or flashy backgrounds.
--> Clean and appropriate clothing; a shirt or suit is recommended.
--> No inappropriate language or behavior.

There is a touch of roleplay: the presentation is addressed to a board,
another company, or a newly hired colleague.
You understand the company’s mission, its market, and general context.

You understand the learner's role, tasks, and responsibilities,
especially if part of a team.
You understand the purpose of their mission in the company’s context.

You understand the outcome: what was achieved, what went well or
didn’t, and whether the work continued after the learner left.

The learner highlights their technical and/or managerial qualities
without exaggeration.

Are their claims (“I can do this,” “I demonstrated that...”)
supported by concrete examples of work done during the experience?
This second point should carry significant weight in your evaluation.
Does the voice sound calm and composed? (More points)
Or is it nervous, hesitant, or overly stressed? (Fewer points)

Are gestures deliberate and supportive of the message? Do facial
expressions and body language convey confidence? Or are there
distracting nervous tics?

sheets.name: zappy
sheets.introduction:
Please respect the following rules:

- Remain polite, courteous, respectful and constructive
throughout the correction process. The well-being of the community
depends on it.

- Identify with the person (or the group) graded the eventual
dysfunctions of the work. Take the time to discuss
and debate the problems you have identified.

- You must consider that there might be some difference in how your
peers might have understood the project's instructions and the
scope of its functionalities. Always keep an open mind and grade
him/her as honestly as possible. The pedagogy is valid only and
only if peer-evaluation is conducted seriously.
sheets.guidelines:
Zappy isn't a trivial project to correct. It is also long project
to grade. For a full project you need to spend around:

- 20-30mn for the server testing
- 10-20mn for the graphic client testing
- 5-10mn to test the client's AI

Between 35 and 60 min in total. Take the necessary time to check out
everything the work of your peer carefully

Enjoy p2p !

body.text: Check firstly the following elements:

items: There is something in the git repository.
The Makefile is present and compiles correctly the executables: server, client and gfx
No cheating (All functions are authorised, the student can explain the code, ...)

body.text:
If an element of this list isn't respected, the grading ends.
Use the appropriate flag. You're allowed to debate some more
about the project, but the grading will not be applied.

sections.title: The server
sections.note: You will have to evaluate the functional and technical quality of the server. A very good understanding of the project is required to properly understand. We will use the following options: ./server -p 4242 -t 10 -x 10 -y 10 -c 5 -n toto titi

body.text: Splitted commands must be concatenated. Test using nc by doing CTRL+D.
Time is properly managed ?
The advance, left and right commands are implemented?
The see/inventory/put/take commands are implemented?
The incantation command is implemented?
The fork command is implemented?
The slots management is correct (-c flag and fork)?

sections.title: Graphic client
sections.note: Are evaluated now both the aesthetic and interactive aspects of the client.

body.text: The client connects properly to the server and displays the map?
Players, stones and food are visible?

Is it possible to click on a square to see details about it
like a floating window, tool tip or something else?

Is it possible to distinguish the number of similar stones on a
square (2 linemate)?

Is it possible to click on a player to see his caracteristics in
a floatting window, tool tip or something else?
Is it possible to scroll through the map?

Is it possible to lock on a player and follow him in his Movements
even if he moves on the map?
Is there a sound management (for the broadcast)?
To ensure a consistent evaluation of AI performance, please use the following map setup during the test

items: Launch server with: ./server -p 4242 -x 10 -y 10 -c 3 -n teamX -t 100
Launch 1 AI client connected to teamX with default parameters
Ensure the server starts with default resource distribution (do not pre-fill the map)

body.text:
It is possible to wait up to 10 mins for the client to level up,
but if after 10 min the AI is still lower than level 8, it means
that it will never reach that level, or because of luck and
luck isn't evaluated here.
Grade depending on the level attained by the AI:

items: level 1/2/3 : 1
level 4/5 : 2
level 6 : 3
level 7 : 4
level 8 : 5

body.text:
At this point of the evaluation, what is your feeling about
the personnal involvment of each member of the group?
The idea here isn't to ask the group but to grade based on
your personnal judgment..

0 -> Only one member of the group seems to have invested time
in the project whatever the reason might be.
1 -> The project seems to be the result of two members of the
group the other ones were just spectating.
2 -> Although the group is argumenting about it you have the
feeling they are bluffing about their involvment.
3 -> One member didn't participate the project.
4 -> One member participated less than the others, but he has
a little idea about the what was done outside of his participation.
5 -> Every member of the group invested time and the final submission
is equally the work of every member.

If one or more members of the groupe dropped out, you can give up to
4 and report the person that didn't invest time at all and is probably
not even present for p2p.
Is the graphic client in 3D ?
Count 1 point per implemented feature.
Live server administration:

items: via the server's shell
via a secured SSL socket
via any kind of authentification
map resizing when with replacement if a player goes out of map
live time update

body.text: Example of other features:

items: sound management in the graphic client
sound management in the AI client
Ghost n' Goblins music (amstrad cpc 6128 version) somewhere in the game
Any other feature you can see!
